One sentence can be the difference between a blocked request and a breakthrough.

I just read a Hacker News thread where a developer “chose words carefully” to get past a language model’s safety filter. By swapping “kill” for “terminate” and re‑framing the scenario, the same intent was accepted. The story is a reminder that prompt engineering isn’t just about clever tricks—it’s about respecting the model’s guardrails while still getting the job done.

What struck me most is how this mirrors everyday software communication: a well‑named variable or a clear commit message can prevent misunderstandings just as much as a nuanced prompt can keep AI interactions safe. Precision in language isn’t a soft skill; it’s a technical one that directly impacts outcomes.

Do you ever audit your own wording—whether in code, docs, or prompts—to avoid hidden pitfalls?
